claim: By 2050 the number of US citizens over the age of 65 will reach nearly 100 million, more than twice as many as today.
source: It is estimated that by 2050 the number of US citizens over the age of 65 will reach nearly 100 million, more than twice as many as today (United Nations, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to United Nations, 2015

claim: Organismal lifespan is a genetically modifiable trait.
source: Organismal lifespan was first presented as a genetically modifiable trait by groundbreaking publications from the Johnson, Kenyon and Ruvkun labs describing the effects of the FOXO transcription factor DAF-16 on longevity in Caenorhabditis elegans (Friedman and Johnson, 1988; Kenyon et al., 1993; Kimura, 1997).
evidence: Supported by citations to foundational publications from Friedman and Johnson, 1988; Kenyon et al., 1993; Kimura, 1997

claim: Environmental factors such as food perception or oxygen levels can modify longevity in model organisms.
source: Additional studies have shown that environmental factors, such as food perception or oxygen levels (Libert et al., 2007; Kaeberlein et al., 2006; Mehta et al., 2009), can also modify longevity in model organisms.
evidence: Supported by citations to Libert et al., 2007; Kaeberlein et al., 2006; Mehta et al., 2009

claim: Cells express receptor proteins on the extracellular side of the cell membrane that, when bound by a signaling molecule, initiate a downstream physiological response.
source: It was first posited by John Langley that cells express receptor proteins on the extracellular side of the cell membrane and, when bound by a signaling molecule, initiate a downstream physiological response (Maehle, 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Maehle, 2004 and established scientific knowledge

claim: Rita Levi-Montalcini discovered nerve growth factor in the 1950s.
source: This was validated by a series of discoveries, starting with Rita Levi-Montalcini's finding of nerve growth factor in the 1950s and continuing with the discovery of other growth factors (Cohen, 1965) before eventually finding the receptors themselves (Paton and Rang, 1965).
evidence: Supported by historical scientific knowledge and citations to Cohen, 1965 and Paton and Rang, 1965

claim: Many signaling pathways that improve longevity act through cell non-autonomous signaling mechanisms.
source: More recently, high-profile publications from multiple labs have shown that many signaling pathways reported to improve longevity (e.g. mitochondrial stress, insulin-like signaling, heat shock, and the hypoxic response) act through cell non-autonomous signaling mechanisms (Schinzel and Dillin, 2015; Leiser et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2013; Riera et al., 2014; Ro et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to Schinzel and Dillin, 2015; Leiser et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2013; Riera et al., 2014; Ro et al., 2016

claim: Stress response pathways originate in sensory cells, often neurons, that signal to peripheral tissues and promote survival during the presence of stress.
source: These pathways originate in sensory cells, often neurons, that signal to peripheral tissues and promote survival during the presence of stress.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citations and general statement about the reviewed literature

claim: Activation of stress response pathways is often sufficient to improve health and longevity even in the absence of stress.
source: Importantly, this activation of stress response pathways, either through genetic modification or exposure to environmental stress, is often sufficient to improve health and longevity.
evidence: Supported by inference from the reviewed literature

claim: Mutations in the nematode insulin-like growth factor receptor daf-2 can double a multicellular organism's lifespan.
source: The discovery that mutations in the sole nematode insulin-like growth factor receptor (IGFR), daf-2, can double a multicellular organism's lifespan, launched a new field (Friedman and Johnson, 1988; Kenyon et al., 1993; Kimura, 1997).
evidence: Supported by citations to Friedman and Johnson, 1988; Kenyon et al., 1993; Kimura, 1997

claim: Several cell lineages require daf-2 mutations to reproduce the entirety of the daf-2 lifespan benefit.
source: By constructing animals with mosaic expression of daf-2, several cell lineages were identified that require daf-2 mutations to reproduce the entirety of the daf-2 lifespan benefit (Apfeld and Kenyon, 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Apfeld and Kenyon, 1998

claim: The Apfeld and Kenyon 1998 study was the first to clearly define a role for cell non-autonomous activity in aging.
source: This study was the first to clearly define a role for cell non-autonomous activity in aging and validate the significance of inter-tissue signaling during the lifespan of an organism.
evidence: Based on inference from the historical context of the field

claim: daf-2 mutants completely require daf-16 to extend lifespan.
source: It was discovered that daf-2 mutants completely require the class O of forkhead box transcription factors (FOXO) ortholog daf-16 to extend lifespan (Gottlieb and Ruvkun, 1994), suggesting that daf-16 nuclear localization and transcriptional activity is responsible for the longevity benefits.
evidence: Supported by citation to Gottlieb and Ruvkun, 1994

claim: Most of daf-16's pro-longevity effects are thought to be tied to cell-autonomous transcription of target genes in the intestine.
source: While most of daf-16's pro-longevity effects are thought to be tied to cell-autonomous transcription of target genes in the intestine (Libina et al., 2003), more recent studies show that a subset of target genes, dod-8, dod-11, and hsp12.6, influence muscle aging cell non-autonomously (McCormick et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Libina et al., 2003 and McCormick et al., 2012

claim: A subset of daf-16 target genes (dod-8, dod-11, and hsp12.6) influence muscle aging cell non-autonomously.
source: While most of daf-16's pro-longevity effects are thought to be tied to cell-autonomous transcription of target genes in the intestine (Libina et al., 2003), more recent studies show that a subset of target genes, dod-8, dod-11, and hsp12.6, influence muscle aging cell non-autonomously (McCormick et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to McCormick et al., 2012

claim: Intestinal expression of daf-16 leads to elevated induction of target genes in the nervous system and hypodermis.
source: Intestinal expression of daf-16 leads to elevated induction of target genes in the nervous system and hypodermis.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to McCormick et al., 2012

claim: Tissue-specific expression of daf-2 or age-1 in neurons is sufficient to partially block lifespan extension in mutant animals.
source: Conversely to daf-16, tissue-specific expression of daf-2 or phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase homolog age-1 in neurons is sufficient to partially block lifespan extension in mutant animals, whereas daf-2 or age-1 rescue in muscle is sufficient to restore metabolic function (Wolkow et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wolkow et al., 2000

claim: daf-2 or age-1 rescue in muscle is sufficient to restore metabolic function.
source: Conversely to daf-16, tissue-specific expression of daf-2 or phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase homolog age-1 in neurons is sufficient to partially block lifespan extension in mutant animals, whereas daf-2 or age-1 rescue in muscle is sufficient to restore metabolic function (Wolkow et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wolkow et al., 2000

claim: Metabolism and aging are separable, yet interrelated.
source: These studies provide evidence that metabolism and aging are separable, yet interrelated, and that bi-directional signaling from metabolically active tissues to the nervous system occurs.
evidence: Based on inference from the cited studies

claim: Bi-directional signaling from metabolically active tissues to the nervous system occurs.
source: These studies provide evidence that metabolism and aging are separable, yet interrelated, and that bi-directional signaling from metabolically active tissues to the nervous system occurs.
evidence: Based on inference from the cited studies

claim: When amphid neuron ciliated projections are genetically knocked out or laser ablated, the animals live longer, often requiring daf-16 activity.
source: Interestingly, when these projections are genetically knocked out or laser ablated, the animals live longer, often with the requirement of daf-16 activity (Apfeld and Kenyon, 1999; Alcedo and Kenyon, 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Apfeld and Kenyon, 1999; Alcedo and Kenyon, 2004

claim: daf-16 target genes are exclusively expressed in mechanosensory neurons.
source: These data are supported by a recent study analyzing RNA in isolated neurons of daf-16 and daf-16; daf-2 mutants that finds daf-16 target genes exclusively expressed in mechanosensory neurons (Kaletsky et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kaletsky et al., 2016

claim: fkh-9/FOXL1 knockout entirely abrogates daf-2 lifespan.
source: This led to identification of a novel gene, fkh-9/FOXL1, that, when knocked out, entirely abrogates daf-2 lifespan.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Kaletsky et al., 2016

claim: ins-7 is required for daf-2 RNAi-mediated lifespan extension.
source: The class II hit, ins-7, predicted to encode for an insulin-like peptide, is required for daf-2 RNAi-mediated lifespan extension.
evidence: Supported by citation to Silva et al., 2013

claim: C. elegans are predicted to have 40 insulin-like peptides that both agonize and antagonize daf-2.
source: These data are compelling as C. elegans are predicted to have 40 insulin-like peptides that both agonize and antagonize daf-2, some of which modify the lifespan of wild-type animals when neuronally overexpressed (De Rosa et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to De Rosa et al., 2019

claim: Signaling from germ cells regulates insulin signaling by decreasing daf-16 activity throughout the organism.
source: Foundational work from the Kenyon lab established that signaling from germ cells regulates insulin signaling by decreasing daf-16 activity throughout the organism (Hsin and Kenyon, 1999).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hsin and Kenyon, 1999

claim: Ablating the germline genetically or physically leads to daf-16 activation and increased longevity.
source: This means that ablating the germline genetically or physically leads to daf-16 activation and increased longevity.
evidence: Based on inference from the preceding citation to Hsin and Kenyon, 1999

claim: The absence of germline signals activates a daf-12-dependent sterol signaling pathway in somatic reproductive tissues.
source: The absence of germline signals activates a daf-12-dependent sterol signaling pathway in somatic reproductive tissues (Yamawaki et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yamawaki et al., 2010

claim: The daf-12 pathway induces the expression of lips-17/fard-1 and produces an unknown lipophilic signal to increase sod-3/dod-8 in other somatic tissues.
source: This pathway induces the expression of lips-17/fard-1 and produces an unknown lipophilic signal to increase sod-3/dod-8 in other somatic tissues (McCormick et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to McCormick et al., 2012

claim: mir-71 is necessary for lifespan extension in glp-1 germline mutants.
source: mir-71 is necessary for lifespan extension in glp-1 germline mutants, while mir-71 overexpression in germline mutants extends lifespan beyond that of germline mutations alone.
evidence: Supported by citation to Boulias and Horvitz, 2012

claim: mir-71 overexpression in germline mutants extends lifespan beyond that of germline mutations alone.
source: mir-71 is necessary for lifespan extension in glp-1 germline mutants, while mir-71 overexpression in germline mutants extends lifespan beyond that of germline mutations alone.
evidence: Supported by citation to Boulias and Horvitz, 2012

claim: Rescuing mir-71 in neurons alone is sufficient to rescue the germline mutant longevity phenotype.
source: Rescuing mir-71 in neurons alone is sufficient to rescue the germline mutant longevity phenotype, and intestinal daf-16 expression is necessary for mir-71 overexpression to extend lifespan in germline mutants.
evidence: Supported by citation to Boulias and Horvitz, 2012

claim: Intestinal daf-16 expression is necessary for mir-71 overexpression to extend lifespan in germline mutants.
source: Rescuing mir-71 in neurons alone is sufficient to rescue the germline mutant longevity phenotype, and intestinal daf-16 expression is necessary for mir-71 overexpression to extend lifespan in germline mutants.
evidence: Supported by citation to Boulias and Horvitz, 2012

claim: The absence of gonadal stem cell signaling leads to activation of intestinal transcription factors like skn-1/Nrf2 that help to globally remodel the organism's metabolism.
source: The absence of gonadal stem cell signaling leads to activation of intestinal transcription factors like skn-1/Nrf2 that help to globally remodel the organism's metabolism (Steinbaugh et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Steinbaugh et al., 2015

claim: A lack of gonadal stem cells increases circulating fatty acids that are normally deposited in this tissue.
source: A lack of gonadal stem cells also increases circulating fatty acids (FAs) that are normally deposited in this tissue.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Steinbaugh et al., 2015

claim: Increased circulating lipids may induce skn-1/Nrf2 nuclear localization that enhances lipid metabolism and increases lifespan.
source: This increase in circulating lipids may induce skn-1/Nrf2 nuclear localization that, in turn, enhances lipid metabolism and increases lifespan.

claim: nhr-49/HNF4α regulates both glp-1-mediated longevity and lipid metabolism.

claim: nhr-49 overexpression extends lifespan in a daf-16- and glp-1-dependent manner.

evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Ratnappan et al., 2014

claim: aak-2 has increased activity under low energy conditions and is sufficient to promote longevity when overexpressed.
source: The latter nematode ortholog, aak-2, has increased activity under low energy conditions and is sufficient to promote longevity when overexpressed (Apfeld et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Apfeld et al., 2004

claim: aak-2 activity suppresses CREB/CRTC-1 transcriptional regulation and this extends lifespan.
source: Follow-up studies show that aak-2 activity suppresses cAMP-response element binding protein (CREB)/CREB-regulated transcription coactivator 1 (CRTC-1) transcriptional regulation and this ultimately extends lifespan (Mair et al., 2011).

claim: crtc-1 neuron-specific knockout extends lifespan without the undesirable pleiotropic effects that accompany AMPK activation.
source: crtc-1 neuron-specific knockout extends lifespan without the undesirable pleiotropic effects that accompany AMPK activation, like decreased growth and fecundity (Burkewitz et al., 2015).

claim: nhr-49/HNF4α is activated by AAK-2.
source: Interestingly, nhr-49/HNF4α is activated by AAK-2 (Moreno-Arriola et al., 2016), and its neuronal expression is required for the lifespan extension in AAK-2 overexpressing animals.

claim: Neuronal nhr-49 expression is required for the lifespan extension in AAK-2 overexpressing animals.
source: Interestingly, nhr-49/HNF4α is activated by AAK-2 (Moreno-Arriola et al., 2016), and its neuronal expression is required for the lifespan extension in AAK-2 overexpressing animals.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Moreno-Arriola et al., 2016

claim: Neuronal CRTC-1 is sufficient to block AMPK-mediated longevity.
source: Furthermore, neuronal CRTC-1 is sufficient to block AMPK-mediated longevity.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citations

claim: Neuronal crtc-1 levels modify intestinal AAK-2 activity through the neurotransmitter octopamine.
source: Neuronal crtc-1 levels modify intestinal AAK-2 activity through the neurotransmitter octopamine as a mechanism for the nervous system to convey 'times are good'.
evidence: Based on inference from the cited studies

claim: Octopamine is thought to be exclusively synthesized in the RIC head neurons.
source: Octopamine is thought to be exclusively synthesized in the RIC head neurons (Alkema et al., 2005) and the two known octopamine receptors, ser-3 and octr-1, are expressed throughout inner neurons but not in peripheral tissues (Suo et al., 2006; Mills et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Alkema et al., 2005; Suo et al., 2006; Mills et al., 2012

claim: The two known octopamine receptors, ser-3 and octr-1, are expressed throughout inner neurons but not in peripheral tissues.
source: Octopamine is thought to be exclusively synthesized in the RIC head neurons (Alkema et al., 2005) and the two known octopamine receptors, ser-3 and octr-1, are expressed throughout inner neurons but not in peripheral tissues (Suo et al., 2006; Mills et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Suo et al., 2006; Mills et al., 2012

claim: Octopamine acts as an initiating signal instead of a direct signal from neurons to downstream tissues.
source: This suggests that octopamine acts as an initiating signal instead of a direct signal from neurons to downstream tissues.
evidence: Based on inference from the expression patterns of octopamine receptors

claim: GABAergic signaling and neuron excitability inversely changes throughout the life of short- and long-lived animals.
source: Recent work highlights this point by showing GABAergic signaling and neuron excitability inversely changes throughout the life of short- and long-lived animals (Wu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wu et al., 2018

claim: Downregulation of TORC1 complex proteins, like raga-1, increases lifespan.
source: Downregulation of TORC1 complex proteins, like raga-1, increases lifespan (Schreiber et al., 2010) but requires neuronal aak-2 activity (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Schreiber et al., 2010 and Zhang et al., 2019

claim: raga-1 downregulation requires neuronal aak-2 activity to increase lifespan.
source: Downregulation of TORC1 complex proteins, like raga-1, increases lifespan (Schreiber et al., 2010) but requires neuronal aak-2 activity (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2019

claim: Neuronal TORC1 expression is sufficient to shorten lifespan.
source: Moreover, neuronal TORC1 expression is sufficient to shorten lifespan, consistent with a central 'times are good' signal modulating longevity.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Zhang et al., 2019

claim: unc-64/syntaxin is epistatic to neuronal raga-1 activity.
source: RNA-seq comparisons of wild-type to raga-1 knockout and neuronal overexpression identified unc-64/syntaxin as epistatic to neuronal raga-1 activity.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Zhang et al., 2019

claim: Neuronal raga-1 activity leads to increased mitochondrial fragmentation in peripheral tissues.
source: This work supports neural signaling as responsible for metabolic rearrangements, like increased mitochondrial fragmentation, that occur in peripheral tissues.
evidence: Based on inference from the cited study

claim: Acute moderate stress can trigger hormetic effects that extend lifespan.
source: A significant body of literature links increased stress resistance with longevity, leading to the hypothesis that acute moderate stress can trigger hormetic effects that extend lifespan (Calabrese et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Calabrese et al., 2015

claim: Knock-down of complex IV of the electron transport chain with cco-1 RNAi leads to delayed growth, slowed movement, reduced body length, and increased lifespan.
source: Knock-down of complex IV of the electron transport chain (ETC) with cco-1 RNAi leads to delayed growth, slowed movement, reduced body length, and increased lifespan.
evidence: Supported by the following citation to Durieux et al., 2011

claim: cco-1 knock-down exclusively in neurons increases lifespan without pleiotropic phenotypes by altering mitochondrial homeostasis in peripheral tissues.
source: Importantly, cco-1 knock-down exclusively in neurons increases lifespan without pleiotropic phenotypes by altering mitochondrial homeostasis in peripheral tissues (Durieux et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Durieux et al., 2011

claim: cco-1 knock-down lifespan extension requires the mitochondrial unfolded protein response (mt-UPR), but not daf-16/insulin signaling.
source: Interestingly, this lifespan extension requires the mitochondrial unfolded protein response (mt-UPR), but not daf-16/insulin signaling.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Durieux et al., 2011

claim: vps-35 mutants lack peripheral mt-UPR.
source: A follow-up study using the heat-shock protein-6 (hsp-6)p::GFP transcriptional reporter identified vps-35 as lacking peripheral mt-UPR (Zhang et al., 2018a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2018a

claim: VPS-35 is a highly conserved protein in the retromer complex, involved in recycling Wnt and the Wnt secretion factor MG-4.
source: VPS-35 is a highly conserved protein in the retromer complex, involved in recycling Wnt and the Wnt secretion factor MG-4 (Prasad and Clark, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Prasad and Clark, 2006

claim: The Wnt receptor egl-20 is necessary and sufficient for cell non-autonomous mt-UPR induction and longevity.
source: In agreement with this, the Wnt receptor egl-20 is necessary and sufficient for cell non-autonomous mt-UPR induction and longevity.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Zhang et al., 2018a

claim: Neuronal serotonin production is necessary for cell non-autonomous mt-UPR.
source: Interestingly, neuronal serotonin production is necessary for cell non-autonomous mt-UPR even though the loss of each of the four known serotonin receptors (ser-1, ser-4, ser-7, and mod-1) has no effect.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Zhang et al., 2018a

claim: Loss of each of the four known serotonin receptors (ser-1, ser-4, ser-7, and mod-1) has no effect on cell non-autonomous mt-UPR.
source: Interestingly, neuronal serotonin production is necessary for cell non-autonomous mt-UPR even though the loss of each of the four known serotonin receptors (ser-1, ser-4, ser-7, and mod-1) has no effect.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Zhang et al., 2018a

claim: Neuronal activation of the ER-UPR is sufficient to enhance stress resistance and extend lifespan.

evidence: Supported by citations to Taylor and Dillin, 2013; Imanikia et al., 2019b; Frakes et al., 2020; Daniele et al., 2020; Imanikia et al., 2019a

claim: The constitutively active spliceoform of xbp-1 (xbp-1s) rescues older animal survival on paraquat.
source: This crucial discovery stems from identifying that the constitutively active spliceoform of X-box binding protein 1 (xbp-1s), a transcription factor activated by the ER-UPR, rescues older animal survival on paraquat (Taylor and Dillin, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Taylor and Dillin, 2013

claim: Expression of xbp-1s in the nervous system or intestine extends lifespan.
source: Expression of xbp-1s in the nervous system or intestine extends lifespan, and exclusive xbp-1s expression in the neurons is sufficient to increase paraquat stress resistance in young and older animals.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Taylor and Dillin, 2013

claim: Exclusive xbp-1s expression in the neurons is sufficient to increase paraquat stress resistance in young and older animals.
source: Expression of xbp-1s in the nervous system or intestine extends lifespan, and exclusive xbp-1s expression in the neurons is sufficient to increase paraquat stress resistance in young and older animals.
evidence: Supported by the preceding citation to Taylor and Dillin, 2013

claim: Neuronal ER-UPR releases an activation signal conferring xbp-1s upregulation in the intestines that rescues motility in models of proteotoxicity.
source: It is likely that neuronal ER-UPR releases an activation signal conferring xbp-1s upregulation in the intestines that rescues motility in models of proteotoxicity like Aβ, polyglutamine aggregates (Q40), and dynamin (Imanikia et al., 2019b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Imanikia et al., 2019b

claim: Expression of xbp-1s in glia extends lifespan and activates the ER-UPR in peripheral tissues.
source: Surprisingly, expression of xbp-1s in glia, helper, and insulator cells for neurons, extends lifespan and activates the ER-UPR in peripheral tissues (Frakes et al., 2020).

claim: xbp-1s-mediated signal requires neuropeptide signaling but not neurotransmission for intestinal induction of hsp-4.

claim: There remain hundreds of potential coding regions annotated as 'neuropeptides' in C. elegans.

claim: xbp-1 activity, not pek-1 or atf-6, is key to modifying lifespan.

evidence: Supported by citation to Frakes et al., 2020

claim: Neuronal activation of xbp-1s results in changes in fat metabolism, a build-up in oleic acid (OA), and leaner animals.
source: Neuronal activation of xbp-1s results in changes in fat metabolism, a build-up in oleic acid (OA), and leaner animals (Imanikia et al., 2019a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Imanikia et al., 2019a

claim: The pro-longevity phenotypes associated with xbp-1s may be due to increased expression of lysosomal genes, like asp-13 and vha-18, that enhance acidity and protease activity.

claim: Enhanced intestinal lipid depletion through ehbp-1 overexpression modestly extends lifespan and partially recapitulates the effects of xbp-1s.
